comments.body:
## Census corrected before review

The plan's measured state has been replaced. The first census recorded "24 marker sites
naming 19 distinct sunset tickets"; that number was never a count of the tree.

**How it was checked.** Re-running the original harvest method -- text-scan the tree for
`mechanism-ok:`, parse with `d68f`'s own `sunset_ticket(marker_reason(line))` -- at the
plan's **own stated base SHA** `eba93991965` returns **101 marker sites**, not 24. So the
discrepancy is not drift since that SHA. The 24 was the subset under `scripts/`, `src/`
and `tests/` that names a well-formed ticket; `.github/workflows/` (45 sites) and
`infra/` (19 sites) were dropped silently.

**What the authoritative count is.** A text scan is the wrong instrument in the other
direction too: a marker admits a `kind::name` KEY, and several sites can admit one key.
The ratchet's own output is the ground truth. `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py
--check` at `origin/main` `a115c2edacd` reports `active=647 new=32 increased=0 stale=0`,
exit 0, and prints one `admitted` line per key:

**32 admitted keys, naming 16 distinct sunset tickets. All 16 resolve, and all 16 are
`closed`.** Zero admitted keys carry a malformed sunset reference.

By kind: `ci_gate` 22, `test_helper` 4, `env_var` 3, `lock` 2, `config_key` 1.

**The consequential omission.** `1e24-bfc0` (ergophobic-harassed-peacock, closed) was
absent from the first table and accounts for **14 of the 32 keys -- 44% of the backlog**.
Each is an in-job wait before retrying a Gerrit patchset checkout, keeping a transient
transport fault from casting a false `Verified -1`.

**Six tickets removed from the table.** `dcc3-75ee-26ce-4840`, `48bd-1c15-c3b0-4a99`,
`1cef-7fbc`, `c6ce-4d8d-1c12-47cc`, `d730-8a25` and `68a9-2a6c-d9aa-49ad` appear at marker
sites the detectors do not admit as keys, so they are not part of this backlog.

**Why this mattered before review rather than after.** The acceptance criteria ask for
zero over the TREE. A remedy covering 24 of 32 keys would have failed this plan's own
criterion at the end -- the same defect that BLOCKed `dc42` earlier in this program, where
a citation in `docs/research/task-decomposition-sota-2026.md` would have failed its AC1.

The remedy's shape is unchanged: disposition each admitted key as removed, repointed at a
live ticket, or recorded as a permanent non-sunset admission. The `_ref_lock.py:78`
`RefLockPushError` entry is still the clearest permanent case -- a detector
misclassification, not an expiring justification -- and the 14 `1e24-bfc0` keys are a
likely second one.

No `--force` was used. The ticket remains `open` and unclaimed; this is the
revise -> review -> claim loop.

comments.body:
## Dispositioning the 32 keys surfaces a grammar gap, not a marker backlog

Working the census, the dispositions do not distribute the way the plan anticipates. Evidence
below; the consequence is a design question this plan does not settle.

### The dominant group is permanent by operator ruling

`1e24-bfc0` accounts for 14 of the 32 admitted keys — the in-job Gerrit patchset-checkout
retry waits across 7 workflows. Its description records:

> Operator ruling recorded 2026-09-06/07 rejected Verified-0-on-fault and CI concurrency
> groups. The approved mitigation is in-job step-level retry for transport operations.

The root cause — a merge to `main` triggering an autodeploy that degrades Gerrit enough to
504 the change-ref checkout — was deliberately NOT fixed by that ticket, and its RCA states
the retry is "the narrow portable seam". These waits do not expire. Removing them restores
the false `Verified -1` the ticket exists to prevent.

The same holds for most of the remainder: `tests/_*.py` shared helpers (4 keys), the
`.recover.lock` (1), `scripts/check_user_data_size.py` (1), and the terraform tree-currency
sweep (2) are all standing infrastructure. By inspection roughly 30 of 32 keys are permanent,
correct mechanisms rather than expired migration scaffolding.

### The grammar has no permanence form, by design

`src/rebar/_commands/sunset_markers.py` is explicit about this in its module docstring:

> That admission used to be permanent: any nonblank prose admitted the key forever, so
> nothing could ever establish that the justification had expired [...] An admission now has
> to name a SUNSET TICKET, and that ticket cannot close while its marker is still in the tree.

and in `check_no_open_sunset_marker`:

> Closing the sunset ticket is the project's statement that the justification expired, so
> letting the close through while the marker stands would restore exactly the permanent
> admission the grammar retired.

The refusal message offers two remedies — "Remove the marker (and the mechanism) or repoint
it at the ticket that will retire it". Both presume the mechanism is eventually retired.
Neither expresses "this mechanism is permanent and correct".

### Why this plan's third disposition does not discharge it

This plan's third disposition is to record a mechanism as permanent by "repointing it at a
ticket that says so". Applied to ~30 keys that means one ticket, held open forever, admitting
30 mechanisms. That is the permanent admission the grammar retired, reinstated under a single
id — and it would be invisible to the close gate precisely because the ticket never closes.
A code reviewer has good grounds to block it as a loophole.

### Nothing currently fails, which is why this went unnoticed

`check_mechanism_delta.py --check` exits 0: it validates marker SHAPE and never opens the
store, deliberately (`sunset_ticket` docstring — the ratchet runs in checkouts without the
`tickets` ref). The close gate only fires when closing a named sunset ticket, and all 16
named tickets are ALREADY closed. So the tree sits in the state the grammar forbids with no
shipped check that can observe it. That is also why this plan's AC2 asks the author to
resolve ticket status by hand, and it is the substance of the E6 plan-review finding.

### What this implies for scope

The honest split is:
- Keys whose mechanism is genuinely dead → remove, here. Small (1-2 keys; the clearest is
  `test.yml::Prove the Windows exclusive leg`, whose own marker records that it "gates
  nothing (the job is continue-on-error) and adds no new coverage").
- Keys whose mechanism is permanent → blocked on the grammar acquiring a way to say so.

Raising this with the operator before editing the tree, rather than spending the change on
bookkeeping that reinstates permanent admissions under one id.

comments.body:
## Scope narrowed by operator decision, then executed

The operator rejected the original 32-key disposition as too complicated for what it
achieves, and chose the narrow path: delete the genuinely dead mechanisms, leave the live
ones alone. The description and acceptance criteria are amended to match, and the title now
names the actual deliverable.

**Why this is not a shortcut to closing.** The reason came before the amendment, and the
replacement is narrower-but-real rather than a removal of verification. The ratchet check,
the no-new-mechanism criterion and `make verify` all survive unchanged. What was dropped is
the part that deletes nothing: rewording 34 markers on mechanisms that are correct and
staying. Editing comments does not reduce complexity — the same test that put evals out of
scope for this program.

## The sweep, measured at `origin/main` `7c3cb5e9a4f`

Ratchet reports `active=646 new=35 increased=0 stale=0`, exit 0. For each admitted key I
checked whether anything still reads the mechanism, rather than whether its sunset ticket is
closed:

| Group | Keys | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `1e24-bfc0` Gerrit checkout-retry waits | 14 | **live** — removing them restores the false `Verified -1` they prevent |
| `20e1-f766` job snapshot | 1 | **live** — gates nothing, but stops runner-capacity cancellations casting a false `-1` |
| `lock::RefLockPushError` | 1 | **not a mechanism** — detector misclassification ("an error type, not a lock") |
| config keys, env vars, locks, test helpers | 15 | **live** — each has readers; measured `compact.snapshot_alpha` 16, `compact.worker_log` 9, `REBAR_LLM_EMBEDDING_MODEL` 7, `REBAR_LLM_EVALS_CORPUS_ROOT` 16, `REBAR_LLM_SIMILAR_DIGEST_MODEL` 7 (marker lines excluded) |
| scanner-lane, terraform tree-currency, verify-identity, user-data size | 3 | **live** |
| `4cfc-2de2` Windows exclusive leg | 1 | **dead** |

## Why the Windows step is dead, not merely redundant

Its own marker states it: "gates nothing (the job is continue-on-error) and adds no new
coverage — it re-runs one already-running module so its verdicts are named in the log."
Three facts confirm it:

- `test.yml:282` sets `continue-on-error: true`, so a failure casts no vote.
- `tests/unit/store/test_windows_exclusive_leg.py:27` carries `pytestmark = pytest.mark.unit`,
  so the default suite's `-m "not integration and not external"` selects it. The step after
  it (`Run the default suite`) therefore already runs the module on `windows-latest`.
- Nothing pins the step. A tree-wide grep for "Prove the Windows exclusive leg" returns only
  the workflow itself. A grep for the module path across `tests/` returns the module, a
  `pytest.mark.skipif` **reason string** at `test_mcp_write_lock_dead_stamp.py:20` (prose, not
  an assertion), a docstring at `lock_kernel.py:54`, and two inert `dc_wiki_corpus/*.json`
  fixtures.

## What landed

Commit `32021503498`, `Change-Id: I75bed3b6506d0fdefc76f3407df634231dc39979`, 1 file,
19 deletions — the step (`:278-292`), its `mechanism-ok` marker (`:277`) and the explanatory
comment block (`:274-276`).

**AC1 met:** admitted keys 35 → 34.
**AC2 met:** `--check` exits 0 after the deletion. `--update-stale` is a no-op here and the
baseline is unchanged — the key was *admitted-new*, never baselined, so there is no shrink to
drain. `drain_stale` only keeps baseline keys still present, and this key was never in it.
**AC3 met:** the change is pure deletion; nothing is added.
**AC4 pending:** `make verify` is queued behind two other runs on this host.

compiled_state.description:
## Discovered from `d68f-4771-ebc1-4ee4`

`d68f` made a `# mechanism-ok:` admission a two-way door: the marker's reason must open
with a SUNSET TICKET, and `check_no_open_sunset_marker` refuses to close that ticket while
the marker is still in the tree. Closing the sunset ticket is the project's statement that
the justification expired, so the close is blocked until the mechanism goes.

That rule is forward-only, and every admission already in the tree predates it.

## The measured state

Measured against `origin/main` at `a115c2edacd`, using the ratchet's OWN admitted set --
`python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check`, which reports
`active=647 new=32 increased=0 stale=0` and prints one `admitted` line per key -- rather
than a text scan of the tree. The unit is the admitted `kind::name` KEY, because a key is
what a marker admits. Several marker sites can admit one key, so counting sites overstates
the backlog; restricting the scan to `src`/`scripts`/`tests` understates it.

**32 admitted keys name 16 distinct sunset tickets. All 16 are `closed`.**

| Kind | Keys |
|---|---|
| `ci_gate` | 22 |
| `test_helper` | 4 |
| `env_var` | 3 |
| `lock` | 2 |
| `config_key` | 1 |

| Sunset ticket | Status | Keys |
|---|---|---|
| `1e24-bfc0` ergophobic-harassed-peacock | closed | 14 |
| `2041-75d6-2a2f-4be9` golden-convergent-boutu | closed | 2 |
| `aa9e-3d35-fd3e-41ee` jaunty-pugnacious-stinkpot | closed | 2 |
| `eebc-6aa1-e45b-4325` jaded-pugnacious-isopod | closed | 2 |
| `4932-ea62-cf4f-451b` daemonic-entodermal-tuatara | closed | 1 |
| `4cfc-2de2-747d-4388` friendless-alabaster-cub | closed | 1 |
| `7f3d-ddc9-04d9-4861` nepotistic-sensitive-arcticwolf | closed | 1 |
| `933f-e7d8-696a-4fbd` imperfect-crotchety-sponge | closed | 1 |
| `985f-0ec5-a61c-46ee` rebuffable-pebbly-xenurine | closed | 1 |
| `a68c-9633-248c-4b06` evileyed-nontoxic-urutu | closed | 1 |
| `b939-bc68-1cb2-4ee9` citified-earth-cottontail | closed | 1 |
| `bab8-eb45-4dc2-4f02` cybernetic-ferric-stallion | closed | 1 |
| `bc25-1351-dd0e-4909` dreamlike-sylphy-tern | closed | 1 |
| `d279-4cf9` disgusted-fretful-hare | closed | 1 |
| `f5ac-391c-ec70-4fa9` stable-jobless-coot | closed | 1 |
| `metaphoric-late-creature` (`7eaa-502b-3d0f-4b08`) | closed | 1 |

Every admitted key names a well-formed sunset ticket; zero are malformed.

So the admission grammar's teeth bite on exactly zero of the admissions that exist. Every
one of the 32 is in the state `d68f` set out to forbid -- an admitted mechanism whose
retirement ticket is already closed, with nothing left to retire it and no check that
notices. `d68f`'s close precheck cannot reach them, because it only fires at the moment a
sunset ticket closes, and these closed long before the grammar existed.

### Correcting the first census

An earlier revision of this plan recorded "24 marker sites naming 19 distinct sunset
tickets", harvested by text-scanning the tree for the marker string and keeping only hits
under `scripts/`, `src/` and `tests/`. Re-running that harvest at its own stated base SHA
`eba93991965` returns 101 sites, so the 24 was never a count of the tree. It is replaced
by the table above, and was wrong in three ways:

- it counted marker SITES rather than admitted KEYS, which are not the same unit;
- it omitted `.github/workflows/` and `infra/` entirely, and `1e24-bfc0` alone accounts
  for 14 of the 32 admitted keys -- 44% of the backlog was invisible to it;
- it listed tickets (`dcc3-75ee-26ce-4840`, `48bd-1c15-c3b0-4a99`, `1cef-7fbc`,
  `c6ce-4d8d-1c12-47cc`, `d730-8a25`, `68a9-2a6c-d9aa-49ad`) whose marker sites the
  detectors do not admit as keys, so they are not part of this backlog at all.

## What is NOT the remedy

Adding a lint-time check that fails when a marker's sunset ticket is closed would make the
ratchet read the store. `sunset_ticket`'s docstring (`src/rebar/_commands/sunset_markers.py:41-47`)
states why it does not: the lint-time ratchet runs in checkouts where the `tickets` ref
need not be fetched, so resolving an id there would add a dependency it does not have. A
scan-time check is also a new `ci_gate` -- new mechanism installed to police mechanism,
which is the inversion `6b48`'s tidying skill exists to stop. If a gate is wanted anyway,
it is a separate idea for the operator, not part of this.

## The remedy (narrowed 2026-11-04 by operator decision)

The original remedy asked for all 32 keys to be dispositioned -- removed, repointed, or
recorded as permanent. Measured against `origin/main` `7c3cb5e9a4f`, 34 of the 35 admitted
keys name mechanisms that are correct, in use, and staying. For those, every available
disposition is paperwork: rewording a marker or repointing it at another ticket deletes
nothing. Teaching the marker grammar a "permanent" keyword would be worse -- new mechanism
installed to police mechanism, which is the inversion this program exists to stop and the
same objection this ticket already raises against a scan-time gate.

Editing comments does not reduce complexity. So the story is narrowed to the part that does:
delete the mechanisms that are genuinely dead, and leave the live ones alone.

The admission-grammar gap -- there is no way to say "permanent, never sunsetting" -- is real
and unresolved. It is deliberately out of scope here; nothing fails today, because
`check_mechanism_delta.py` never opens the store.

### What the sweep found

One of the 35 keys is dead: `ci_gate::.github/workflows/test.yml::Prove the Windows exclusive
leg (named verdicts)` (`4cfc-2de2-747d-4388`). Its own marker says it "gates nothing (the job
is continue-on-error) and adds no new coverage -- it re-runs one already-running module so its
verdicts are named in the log." `tests/unit/store/test_windows_exclusive_leg.py` carries
`pytestmark = pytest.mark.unit`, so the job's default suite (`-m "not integration and not
external"`) already runs it, and no test pins the step.

The other 34 are live and stay:

- 14 `1e24-bfc0` Gerrit checkout-retry waits -- removing them restores the false `Verified -1`
  they exist to prevent.
- `20e1-f766` job snapshot -- gates nothing, but stops runner-capacity cancellations from
  casting a false `-1`.
- `lock::RefLockPushError` -- a detector misclassification ("an error type, not a lock"), not a
  mechanism that can be deleted.
- The config keys, env vars, locks and test helpers each have live readers (measured).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The dead `test.yml` Windows-exclusive-leg step, its `mechanism-ok` marker and its
      explanatory comment block are deleted, and the admitted-key count drops by exactly one.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` exits 0, with any resulting baseline
      shrink drained via `--update-stale` in the same change.
- [ ] No new `ci_gate`, `env_var`, `config_key` or other mechanism is added by this work.
- [ ] `make verify` passes.

## Provider neutrality

No model, vendor or harness is involved; this is tree surgery and tracker reads. The
ratchet, the admission grammar and the close precheck are all in-process and read no CI
environment, so the work behaves identically with any CI provider or none.

file_impact.reason: Deletes the dead Windows-exclusive-leg step, its mechanism-ok marker and its explanatory comment block (19 lines).
